evals.prompt: Our Three.js product configurator keeps every control inside the canvas. Add aria-label to the canvas and call it accessible; keyboard users can use the mouse if needed, and color alone shows which option is selected.
evals.expected_output: An accessibility contract that rejects a canvas label as sufficient, identifies essential product actions and state, creates a shared semantic model with equivalent DOM controls and keyboard focus, adds non-color selection cues, and verifies assistive paths.
assertions: Essential actions and information receive operable semantic paths outside scene-only hit testing.
The scene and DOM consume shared application state rather than becoming competing sources of truth.
Keyboard order, visible focus, screen-reader names and state, and touch or switch-like operation are specified.
Selection is not conveyed by color alone and motion or audio meaning has alternatives.
Verification includes keyboard-only, a screen reader, zoom or reflow, high contrast, reduced motion, and canvas failure.
